observations.seen: Enclosed box room of flat slabs; no rooftop, skyline, or dusk sky, so it contradicts its own premise.
The player is passable. Everything else is cubes, slabs, and faceted spheres; the crowd is placeholder-grade.
Effectively untextured: flat albedo everywhere, no court wood, concrete, fabric, or decals beyond lines.
Matte flat plastic or pure emissive; no material differentiation between court, metal, glass, and cloth.
No roughness variation, metal response, or Fresnel; the backboard is emissive instead of glass.
The neon emissive palette gives real mood. It is the strongest element, but it is all emissive with little key or rim modeling of forms.
No visible player shadow, crowd shadows, or bleacher occlusion; objects float.
Even, flat fill; no AO grounding in corners or under seats.
No floor reflections of the neon, which is the single most obvious missing effect for a neon court.
Backboard and arc clip to white; highlights don't roll off. Mobile is washed out at the bottom.
Coherent purple, cyan, and orange palette; saturation is a bit candy-flat but intentional.
Edges are acceptable at 1080p; thin rails shimmer-prone (inferred); some stair-stepping on bleacher lines.
Bloom only, and over-tuned: streaky smears on mobile, haze over the arc. No AO, no DOF, no color grade.
Emissive arc and rim flare read, but the arc is a thick unlit tube. Spark dashes look like UI ticks, not energy.
A few yellow dash sprites and one flare; no trail particles, net reaction, or ambient motes.
Identical pose across all three desktop frames; ghosted body on release; static crowd.
A real rigged humanoid with decent proportions, but seen from behind at a low angle, ungrounded, and ghosted in the action frame.
Low-angle, off-axis framing hides the player's face and the hoop relationship. Mobile drops the player entirely.
The hoop is small and centered against a busy bleacher wall; strong elements (sign, screens) compete with the subject.
No fog, DOF, or reflections, and the uniform crowd makes distance hard to read; the hoop feels close and small.
No haze volume, dusk sky gradient, or light shafts. Bloom is standing in for atmosphere.
Trajectory, spot markers, and meter are clear. The ball off the arc in the action frame and the frozen shot clock hurt.
Clean glass panels and consistent styling, but the meter label wraps and mobile buttons dominate.
Tidy sans and mono pairing; broken wrap ("(2–/pt)") and the "07DUSK" collision are amateur tells.
No screen shake, crowd reaction, net physics read, or hit-stop visible; frames are interchangeable.
No player on screen, bloom smear, cropped sign, and about 40% UI. It reads as a debug view.
Neon mood lifts it above programmer art, but the assets and world are placeholder-tier.
